The CropSim v8.0 source fortran/original/CROPSIM_V8.0.F90 was not changed. A copy was built with the same three parity edits used by the repo's test harness (run-folder path, path separators, resetting three module settings between soils) plus WRITE-only trace calls.
The traced build's yearly, monthly, precipitation and initial-condition outputs are byte-identical to an untraced build of the same copy, so tracing did not change any result.
Every number on this page is a value the Fortran computed and wrote to the trace. The page does no arithmetic of its own, apart from rounding for display.
105 of 105 values cross-checked against the model's own daily printout for this week (debug print level 3) agree.
Weather: Scottsbluff station files for 2017 (spin-up) and 2018 (shown). Reference ET in these files is Hargreaves (ETRHG), not Penman-Monteith. The week is 10–16 July 2018 (days 191–197).
Location is western rather than central Nebraska because the central Nebraska weather files were not reachable (still archived in OneDrive). Heath approved using the western set.
Soil is a representative profile, not a mapped SSURGO component: 10 one-foot layers, field capacity 0.28–0.26 and wilting point 0.11–0.09 in/in, hydrologic group B, curve number table 67/78/85/89.

Crop and irrigation settings: corn with demand (management allowed depletion) scheduling, a 1.10 in gross application at 0.85 efficiency, system capacity of 0.30 in/day running 90% of the time, and a 0.25 in rain allowance. Block and tillage files are the repo test fixtures.

Initial condition: profile at 85% of available water on 1 January 2017, then one full year of spin-up. The dry 2017 left the deep profile well below field capacity, which is why no deep percolation occurs in 2018.
